The 3 things they don't want you to know about AI.

Takes 30 seconds. 🧵

1. The free version is enough to start.

You don't need a paid plan or a course to get real work done today.

2. It's only as good as what you tell it.

"Write an email" gets you something generic.

"I own a bakery. A customer's order was late. Write a short apology and offer 10% off."

gets you something you'd actually send.

3. Make it ask you questions first.

Add this to any request:

"Before you answer, ask me 3 questions."

The answer gets noticeably better.

It can be wrong.

It sounds confident either way. Read everything before you send it.

Try one of these today.

The prompts small business owners actually use.

Copy, paste, fill in the brackets. Works in Claude or ChatGPT. 🧵

1. Reply to a customer

"Reply to this customer. Short and friendly. Answer the question and offer a time to book: [message]"

2. Follow up on a quote

"Write a 2 sentence follow up on a quote I sent 3 days ago. No pressure."

3. Ask for a review

"Write a short text asking a happy customer for a Google review. Keep it casual."

4. Handle a price objection

"A customer says I'm too expensive. Help me explain my price clearly and politely."

5. Plan the day

"Here's my to do list. Order it by what brings in money first: [list]"

6. Answer a bad review

"Write a calm, professional reply to this review: [review]"

7. Write captions

"Give me 5 short captions about [what I did today]. Plain language, no hashtags."

8. Set it up once

"Ask me 5 questions about my business, then write instructions so you always answer the way I would."

That's a Business Brain.

AI for beginners. Lesson 1: how to use Claude.

10 steps. No tech terms. 🧵

1. Go to claude.ai or download the app.

Sign up free with your email.

2. Write like you're texting a capable assistant.

No special wording needed. Say what you need.

3. Tell it who you are.

"I run a cleaning business in Miami."

One line of context changes every answer.

4. Paste things in.

Emails, reviews, your menu, a photo of a receipt. It can read them.

5. Ask for changes.

"Shorter." "Friendlier." "More like how I talk." It rewrites in seconds.

6. Have it ask questions first.

"Ask me 3 questions before you answer."

7. Save your details once.

Put them in a Project so every chat already knows them.

8. Check before you send.

It's fast, not perfect. Read every word.

That's lesson 1.

Lesson 2: how to write a prompt that actually works.

Four parts. Use them every time. 🧵

1. Say who you are.

"I run a small landscaping business."

Context changes everything that comes after.

2. Say exactly what you want.

Not "write something". Name the thing.

"Write a text to a customer whose job is delayed by rain."

3. Add the details only you know.

"New date is Thursday. No extra charge. Keep it friendly."

4. Say how it should look.

"Under 50 words. No emojis."

Put together:

"I run a small landscaping business. Write a text to a customer whose job is delayed by rain. New date is Thursday, no extra charge. Friendly, under 50 words, no emojis."

That's lesson 2.

Bookmark it and try it on your next real message. Lesson 3: five things to try with AI today.

Lesson 3: five things to try with AI today.

Each one takes under a minute. 🧵

1. Explain a confusing email.

"Explain this in 3 sentences. What do I need to do?"

2. Answer a hard message.

"Help me reply to this. Polite, short, firm."

3. Read a photo.

Snap a receipt, a whiteboard or a handwritten note.

"Type this up as a list."

4. Plan your day.

"Here's my to do list. Order it by what matters most."

5. Get a second opinion.

"Here's my plan. What could go wrong?"

That's lesson 3.

Pick one and do it today. Lesson 4: how to make AI sound like you.

Lesson 4: how to make AI sound like you.

So nobody can tell. 🧵

1. Show, don't describe.

Paste 2 or 3 messages you actually wrote.

"Write like this."

2. Ban the AI words.

"Don't use: delve, elevate, seamless, I hope this finds you well."

3. Set the length.

AI rambles by default. Give it a limit.

"Two sentences max."

4. Ask it to rewrite casually.

"Make this sound like a text, not an email."

5. Save it once.

Put your examples in a Claude Project so every chat starts in your voice.

That's lesson 4.

Lesson 5: how to check AI's work.

It can sound sure and still be wrong. 🧵

1. Check names, numbers and dates.

That's where mistakes hide.

2. Ask how sure it is.

"How confident are you? What should I double check?"

3. Ask where it got that.

"What's your source for this?"

If it can't say, verify it yourself.

4. Turn on web search for anything recent.

Without it, AI only knows what it learned up to a cutoff date.

5. You send it, you own it.

Read every word before it goes to a customer.

That's lesson 5.
